content: Excel does not reliably detect UTF-8 in a CSV without a BOM; accented characters (Spanish ñ, á, é) render as mojibake (Microsoft support 'Opening CSV UTF-8 files correctly in Excel'; SO 6588068 'both Windows and Mac users get garbage characters'). Fix: emit UTF-8 with BOM (EF BB BF) or offer xlsx. Delimiter is locale-dependent: Excel in Spanish/European locales uses ';' as the list separator, so comma-separated output collapses into one column - emitting sep=; breaks the BOM unless the BOM comes first. Excel also strips leading zeros from numeric-looking fields (Watermark support 'Preparing Data for CSV-UTF-8 Imports'), which matters for squad numbers, so quote/force text formatting. Streams/raw text avoids spreadsheet auto-conversion rewriting long digits.
